title: Liverpool vs. Arsenal Player Ratings: 14-Year Spell Broken in Statement Showing
subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By James Cormack1:55 PM ESTArsenal claimed their first win at Anfield since 2012.  / David Price/Arsenal FC/Getty ImagesThe champions earned a statement result at Anfield on Sunday afternoon, with Kai Havertz’s early goal proving enough for Arsenal to claim victory away to Liverpool for the first time in the Premier League since 2012.

Havertz’s back-post conversion from Declan Rice’s pinpoint cross came amid a bright opening to the contest from the away side, desperate to respond from their midweek defeat at League Two Fleetwood Town.

However, the goal burst the in-form hosts into life, with Arsenal forced to navigate wave after wave of Liverpool pressure. An incredibly watchable affair played out, as the Gunners offered a threat on the counter and came ever so close to doubling their lead, only for Jurriën Timber to inadvertently deny Havertz from reaching Noni Madueke’s knockdown on the goal line.

The Reds’ should’ve restored parity before the break, but Alexis Mac Allister headed over from Milos Kerkez’s cross. That moment was the best Liverpool would produce, with Arsenal limiting the chaos that defined the contest after Havertz’s goal. Control was restored, and their stubborn defense settled in.
In truth, Liverpool struggled to muster a clear-cut chance as they chased an equalizer; Arsenal saw out their advantage with relative comfort to earn a huge victory on Merseyside.

The Gunners secured a rare victory at Anfield. / David Price/Arsenal FC/Getty ImagesThe champions visited a ground they haven’t won at in 14 years, when manager Mikel Arteta started alongside Santi Cazorla and Abou Diaby in midfield. Lukas Podolski was Arsenal’s hero on that occasion, and it was another German who rose to the occasion on Sunday to deliver an all-too-rare victory.

The Gunners arrived on Merseyside off the back of a chastening humiliation at Fleetwood Town—one of the great League Cup upsets. A trip to Liverpool seemed suboptimal, given the context, especially with the optimistic mood surrounding Andoni Iraola’s side at the moment.

But Arsenal have ascended to such heights under this manager because they’re made of sterner stuff. Their capacity to bounce back from adversity is admirable, and the character of Arteta’s roster was laid bare at a ground where so many of their dreams have died in the past.

There were times when they threatened to wilt, with Liverpool producing sequences and phases of soccer reminiscent of the team that captured hearts and minds when Jürgen Klopp was beating his chest on the Anfield touchline. They were fortunate to remain ahead at halftime, but the interval provided scope to reset.

The second half was played on the champions’ terms, and as Liverpool grew more desperate, Arsenal only looked more settled. The Reds’ ran out of puff while the Gunners’ stature remained erect. This was a statement victory, and a reminder that Arteta’s champions are the team to beat.
Barcola’s pace is such a threat. / Robbie Jay Barratt/AMA/Getty Images*Ratings provided by FotMob*
GK: Alisson—5.8: It was ultimately Jacquet who gave away possession, but the young center back wasn’t helped by a hospital pass from his goalkeeper. Made a superb save to deny Christos Tzolis.
RB: Ronald Araújo—7.0: A tone-setter in this Liverpool team. Araújo’s impressive run of form continued here.
CB: Jérémy Jacquet—6.6: Wasn’t great for the opening goal, but was among those to recover from tricky starts to the contest.
CB: Virgil van Dijk—7.5: Van Dijk was a steady head throughout the contest, helping Liverpool sustain pressure.

LB: Milos Kerkez—7.3: Kerkez at least proved, with a couple of excellent deliveries, that he could serve as a useful attacking outlet. Offered admirable endeavour, yet continues to leave plenty to be desired defensively.
CM: Trey Nyoni—6.5: The youngster overcame a tough start, during which he was fortunate not to be booked, to settle nicely into proceedings. Adds a level of composure to Liverpool’s midfield.
CM: Alexis Mac Allister—7.1: Really good amid Liverpool’s first-half surge, only to miss a gilt-edged chance, their best of the game, before the interval.
RW: Bradley Barcola—6.0: A couple of loose touches prevented Barcola from having a clearer sight of goal at times, and he faded after a sharp start.
